summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's confidential launch data, find where the plan contradicts reality, and build a general, versioned recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, reconcile, supplier emails with approval) with a Today/Launch UI.
summary.outcome: Found the key discrepancies (overbooked art books, failed statue lot, sleeve revision conflict, frozen shipment list, Karton offer). Built and committed a working app: polling, reconciled shipment tracking, site questions with a count page, approver routing, routines polish and editable email review. Sent real follow-up emails to suppliers and pushed 16 commits.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Files are replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare SHA-256, not just filenames.
Confidential data lives in gitignored data/ and .env; only .env.example is committed. Values from the data must never go into code.
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change; a session with no repo edits logs 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint'.
Team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.

open_shipments.csv is not SAP and contradicts the slides. It stopped updating at Fri 20 Nov 17:00. The hand-kept Excel tracker was read only by the verifier until the tracking builder made it a source.

Shipment status precedence is goods receipt, then site answer, then supplier doc or reply, then hand-kept tracker (only if newer), then system export, then other sheets. Silence is measured against the clock from any source.
Supplier emails may only go to known addresses (profile contact or prior reply senders). This guards against forged-notice fraud and unregistered senders.
Supplier profiles hold full contact names (e.g. Agnieszka Nowak). Hand-written emails must use them instead of guessing a title from the address.
Lid magnet shortage is a false alarm: PackRight fits the magnets into the box.
Recognizer does not read Word files, so the CPO memo remains unread.

code.finding: A _MONEY regex further down in the file overrides an earlier one with the same name; the new regex had to be renamed. Card status is only final late in build_cards, so routing rules must run after that point.

Generic site-question model (packed/received/count) with tokenised phone count page, OCR suggestion, backflush of book stock and env-tunable thresholds (ASK_PACKOUT_STALE_HOURS, ASK_COUNT_MARGIN etc.).
Reconciled shipment status and frozen-list card. The old silent_shipments in routines.py measured silence against the newest list entry, which hid a frozen list.
floor.receipts() treats any receipt on the same order and part as booked regardless of date, so an old delivery could hide a site question (TODO left).

workflow: Parallel builders can edit the same shared files (api.py), so commits had to wait for all builders to report and be split carefully.
Paid image-recognition calls of a few cents are now standing-approved; this is saved in the ask-before-spending memory.
Real outward-facing actions (supplier emails, pushes) were confirmed with the user first, and nothing was sent on the user's behalf without approval.
Avoid sending multiple emails to one supplier within minutes; Lio warns that spammed suppliers may stop cooperating.

friction: Portal token was empty at the start, which blocked data access until the user supplied it.
Three hand-written supplier emails greeted the wrong names ('Mr Nowak', 'Mr Rohan') because they were guessed from addresses; no correction was sent to avoid more noise.
Stray night-time emails to Hwaseong were sent by routines.
Two builders editing api.py concurrently prevented clean partial commits.
Scanned PDFs and Word files need rendering or special handling; the recognizer cannot read DOCX.
The 14:00 briefing page and doc went stale after the 14:37 drop and later changes.
